title: The typed reader refuses a pointer value whose own type is const-qualified (T *const) and a void* bit-cast value
why: W47-TYPED-ROOT-DECLARATION-READER measured the twelve frozen-forecast misses W47-ACCESS-PATH-POSITIONS attributed to the lexical declaration reader (docs/reports/w47-typed-root-declaration-reader/artifacts/cause/): for all twelve the lexical reader is readable, every root is never bound and not may_bind, and the typed reader refuses with every premise granted. Eight returns refuse because the value's own type is `T *const` (a pointer member read through a `const` pointee, or an element of a `T *const[]` member): rd_kafka_Node_host, rd_kafka_Node_rack, rd_kafka_mock_cluster_bootstraps, rd_kafka_mock_cluster_handle, rd_kafka_opaque, rd_kafka_handle_mock_cluster, rd_kafka_messages_get, rd_kafka_share_partition_offsets_list_get; `typed_access_path::is_pointer` requires the type text to end in `*`. The two rd_kafka_topic_partition_get_(current_)leader_epoch getters, whose declared-local premise rule 10l now answers, refuse on `parpriv = rktpar->_private`: an ImplicitCastExpr BitCast from `void *` (which `strip` refuses) over a `void *const` member. The P3 control a_redeclared_typedef_formal_keeps_the_pointer_return_refusal refuses for the same `char *const` reason. rd_kafka_ConfigEntry_name and rd_kafka_share_partition_offsets_offsets return an array member by decay and stay refused by rule 5j. DISCHARGE: a positively typed pointer value whose only difference is a top-level qualifier on the value (and, separately, a bit-cast from `void *` to an object pointer in a pointer-destination statement) admitted by a rule that keeps every per-hop obligation and rule 5b's premise, with matching audited Lean, negative controls (volatile/_Atomic pointers, casts to non-object types, casts in the middle of a path) and a measured corpus/system re-pin naming which of the ten become Safe.

title: The lexical untracked-base closure does not see an assignment nested in a condition or a for clause
why: borrowed_actual::untracked_bases reads assignments with a top-level `=` of a `;{}`-delimited token run, so `if (!(p = f()))`, `while ((p = next(q)))` and `for (p = f(); ...)` never make `p` risky, although the body binds `p` from a call. Rule 10l's side-by-side parity (docs/reports/w47-typed-root-declaration-reader/artifacts/after/root-declarations/) measured, in functions the lexical reader reads (where its answer is served, unchanged), 119 name records the AST closure binds from a call in a nested assignment while the lexical closure calls them never bound; 33 are roots of admitted typed rows (never-bound chains), all in non-Safe functions. No Safe function rests on such a root: the three Safe functions with a disputed root are rule 5l container_of bindings (mk_fifo_queue_get, mk_plugin_cap) and a scalar-array sub-object store (rd_kafka_Uuid_str), where the AST reader is the over-conservative side. The same records show the lexical closure's other blind spots the AST names (a later declarator initialised from an earlier one, 177 copies of AST-bound names). DISCHARGE: the lexical closure reads nested and later-declarator assignments (or the typed premises read the AST-joined answer in every function), with every Safe -> non-Safe move named as a correction in a measured re-pin, and matching Lean.
